summary.one_liner: The 37signals employee handbook, a public document describing the company's policies, benefits, culture, and job titles.
summary.what_it_does: The README is the text of 37signals' internal employee handbook, published as a repository. It lists the handbook's sections: getting started, benefits and perks, how the company works, career progression, rituals, managing work devices, internal systems, moonlighting policy, state leave provisions, severance packages, and job titles for designers, ops, programmers, QA, and support. The README itself contains only the table of contents and a short introduction; the actual section content is not included in the README text provided. It notes that the handbook may change at any time and that the repo can be watched to follow updates. It directs questions to the People Ops team or a manager.
use_cases: Looking up 37signals company policies and benefits
Studying an example of a public company employee handbook
Reviewing job title frameworks for designers, programmers, QA, ops, and support
Finding severance and state leave policy examples
Tracking changes to a company handbook through a git repo
notable: Public employee handbook from the company behind Basecamp and HEY
Covers job title definitions by discipline (design, ops, programming, QA, support)
Includes policies on moonlighting, severance, and state-specific leave
Changes can be followed through the GitHub repository history
caveats: The README contains only the section list and intro; the policy text is not in the README provided
Handbook may be updated at any time, so content can change
Not a software project; there is nothing to install or run
